evidence: "stated here at first use, defined in full at Ch 8 §8.3.3"
issue: Section reference 'Ch 8 §8.3.3' violates the book's own cross-reference convention stated on PDF p.19: "Do not repeat a chapter number after the chapter name — write Ch. 8 § 3 or § 8.3.3, not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3." The chapter number 8 appears both before and inside the section reference.
fix_instruction: Change to '§ 8.3.3' (standalone) or 'Ch. 8 § 3.3' (chapter-first, section number only), per the stated convention.

evidence: "not the per-host aggregate rate of ~19,800 tok/s — see Ch 8 §8.3.4"
issue: Section reference 'Ch 8 §8.3.4' violates the same cross-reference convention (PDF p.19: 'not Ch. 8 § 8.3.3'). The chapter number 8 appears before and inside the reference. This is the second instance of the same defect pattern.
fix_instruction: Change to '§ 8.3.4' or 'Ch. 8 § 4' per the stated convention.

evidence: "read any 'meets 1.2 s' statement as conditional on a named tested workload and end-to-end timing (S-01)"
issue: S-01 is referenced as a parenthetical shorthand but is never defined or introduced anywhere in the Preface or preceding chapters visible in the document. A reader encountering it here has no way to resolve the reference without reaching Chapter 14 (benchmarking protocol) approximately 240 pages later, and there is no forward-pointing explanation (e.g., 'S-01, defined in Ch. 14').
fix_instruction: Either define S-01 at first use with a brief parenthetical (e.g., '(S-01, the Chapter 14 benchmark scenario)'), or add an explicit forward pointer such as '(S-01; defined in Ch. 14 § 1).'

evidence: "important not because a single kilowatt-hour is meaningful by itself, but because every downstream cost and capacity number is denominated in it — or, for non-autoregressive generation, in model evaluations"
issue: Ambiguous pronoun 'it' in 'denominated in it': the nearest antecedent is 'a single kilowatt-hour' (inside the dash-enclosed clause), but the intended referent is 'a token' (the sentence's overall subject/metaphor). A reader parsing linearly may momentarily resolve 'it' to kilowatt-hour before correcting.
fix_instruction: Replace 'denominated in it' with an explicit noun: 'denominated in tokens' (or 'denominated in a token').

evidence: "The KV budget on a nominal 24 GB device is therefore 20 GB (24 − 4)."
issue: Label 'KV budget' for 20 GB is misleading. The 20 GB (24 − 4 reserve) is the budget for weights + KV combined; after the 16 GB of weights are subtracted, only 4 GB remains available for KV. A reader may interpret 20 GB as space available for KV alone, which would be a 5× overestimate of actual KV headroom. The subsequent statement that the device passes (total 21.245 GB < 24 GB) is correct, but the label on the intermediate quantity is imprecise.
fix_instruction: Rename to 'weights + KV budget after reserve' or 'model budget after reserve' (20 GB), or state the actual KV-available space: '24 − 4 − 16 = 4 GB available for KV.'

evidence: "MLA ≈57× less for DeepSeek-class geometry, inside a ~50–60× band"
issue: Phrasing '57× less' is technically imprecise under ASD-STE100: 'X× less' is ambiguous (subtract X times? or divide by X?). The correct technical phrasing is '57× smaller' or '1/57th the size.' This pattern recurs at least twice more: '~5.5× less compute' (PDF p.61, Ch.3 §3.3.3) and '~12× less per-token weight traffic' (PDF p.67, Ch.3 §3.6.1).
fix_instruction: Replace all 'X× less' with 'X× smaller' or rephrase as 'reduced by a factor of X' / '1/X the size.' Scan full document for remaining instances.
